newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar invested $17.8 billion in energy, minister.
newsitem.headline: Qatar invested $17.8 billion in energy, minister.

text.p: Qatar said on Saturday it had invested $17.85 billion in the oil and gas sector in the past four years to boost production capacity and exploit enormous gas reserves.

"We have invested 65 billion riyals ($17.85 billion) during the past four years to develop the oil and gas sector", Qatar's Minister of Energy and Industry, Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah, told reporters.
Qatar, the smallest producer in the 11-member Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, has an OPEC quota of 378,000 barrels a day, but has generally been assumed to produce around 500,000 b/d.
"Hopefully we'll reach 700,000 b/d by 2000," al-Attiyah said.
The country has, during the past four years, signed production sharing agreements with a number of Western oil companies to expand its production capacity.
Qatar, which has the world's third largest gas reserves, has invested heavily in a number of petrochemical and fertilisers projects in partnership with foreign companies.
